stages.title: The question
stages.desc: The analyst lists seven states and asks who pays once cooking starts.
stages.narration: Day one. The analyst agent asks the question the kickoff skipped.

stages.title: Screen only
stages.desc: Today the rule lives in OrderTrackingState.canCancel. The domain accepts any status.
stages.narration: Today the rule is only in the screen. The domain accepts anything.

stages.title: Into the domain
stages.desc: Order.canBeCancelled on the entity. cancelOrder fails when it is false.
stages.narration: The architect moves the rule onto the order entity. The screen reads it.

stages.title: AC-3 goes green
stages.desc: The testing agent wrote AC-3 from the requirement. It failed, then passed.
stages.narration: The test written from the requirement fails, then passes. Two layers done.

stages.title: The rules say any value
stages.desc: Customers may change status, timeline and isRated. To anything, from anything.
stages.narration: Then the security agent reads the rules. A customer can write any status.

stages.title: Check the transition
stages.desc: To cancelled only from placed or confirmed. Rating stays separate.
stages.narration: The fix checks the transition, not just which fields change.

stages.title: Two attacks, every push
stages.desc: Customer cancels own preparing order: denied. Customer sets delivered: denied.
stages.narration: The pen test agent adds two attacks that run on every push.

stages.title: Shipped, three layers
stages.desc: Plus one ICU message, a named close button, user-language notes, order_cancelled.
stages.narration: Day three, it ships. The rule holds in screen, domain, and rules.

stages.title: One rule, every layer
stages.desc: The handoffs are the workflow. Start with four agents.

end.title: One rule. Every layer.
end.sub: A cancel can arrive through the screen, the domain or Firestore directly. Guard all three.

post.caption:
One feature. Fourteen AI agents. One rule that had to hold in three places. 🧭

"Users can cancel an order" in a Flutter and Firebase app:
1️⃣ The analyst agent asks who pays once cooking starts. A person answers: cancel only before preparing.
2️⃣ The architect moves the rule from one screen onto the Order entity.
3️⃣ The testing agent's AC-3, written from the requirement, fails, then passes.
4️⃣ The security agent reads the Firestore rules: a customer may change status on their own order to any value, from any state. Direct writes bypass the domain entirely.
5️⃣ The fix checks the transition. The pen test agent adds two attacks that run on every push.

Screen, domain, database. A business rule has to hold wherever a request can arrive.
